routes.name: codex-sandboxed-subscription
routes.note: A NATIVE-SANDBOX ROUTE, and the reason worker_io exists. The args are the measured filesystem boundary: a permission profile that reads everywhere, denies the operator's credential stores and the shared stack, and grants write nowhere - the adapter adds the task root and both clones' .git directories at launch, because only the launch knows them, and because this harness marks .git read-only inside a workspace-write root by default. Egress is deliberately OFF: the operator has not ruled on whether destination-scoped networking satisfies the P4 risk, and a supervised worker does not need it. worker_io is 'supervised' because inside that sandbox the container socket, the workspace hub and every forge credential are unreachable - so the supervisor performs this worker's emits, its workspace sync and its publications from outside the boundary. That is a stronger deployment, not a weaker one.

routes.name: example-api-route

price_basis.source: example vendor list prices, first-party pricing page

routes.note: TWO THINGS AT ONCE. It is a harness this build has never heard of, launching on the built-in 'generic' adapter from configuration alone - so a new CLI, a wrapper script, a container invocation or a VM entry point needs no code change to become runnable, at the honest cost that its model identity is recorded as declared and its usage as unavailable. And it bills against the api market with a provider credential inherited BY NAME: provider access is deployment posture and the operator's to decide. What may never be inherited under any configuration is a Hive authority credential - the database, gateway and reserved-role DSNs - which refuses at catalog load. The price_basis is what makes a historical cost derivable later without consulting a catalog that has since changed.
